title.narrative: Integrated Health Program (IHP) Task Order Five (TO5)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Provide health system support to the Sokoto state government to plan, budget and coordinate the implementation of primary health care services and advocate for improved health system governance. .Build the capacity of healthcare workers to provide quality, equitable primary health services and to reach underserved populations. .Issue small grants to local organizations to provide technical assistance and capacity building support to health facilities in provision of nutrition services, gender based violence (GBV) and informal sector enrollment in financial risk protection schemes. .Promote the adoption of essential WASH actions such as environmental hygiene handwashing and safe disposal of waste at the facility levels in Sokoto State..Collaborate with government stakeholders to strengthen facility-level results reporting, use of data for decision making,service quality improvement and develop a comprehensive Annual Operational Plan for Sokoto State, focusing on high impact interventions. .This activity will strengthen health systems and increase access to and improve the quality of primary health care services in Sokoto State. It will work via a multipartite MOU between the Sokoto State Government, USAID Nigeria, Gates Foundation, Global Affairs Canada, Dangote Foundation, and UNICEF, to reduce maternal and child mortality in Sokoto, and to increase public and private health systems' skills to sustainably supervise and manage quality primary health care services. .This activity contributes to USAID priorities by focusing on evidence-based interventions, sustainability, localization and capacity building. It also contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the Embassy's ICS, and is closely aligned with Goal 3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan...
